reply_text:
I reviewed the two commits on `leaderboard-sort` and didn't change any code. **I'd hold the merge until one bug is fixed.**

**Must fix: ranking breaks on large scores** (`src/rank.js`)
The sort uses `b.score - a.score`. That turns the score strings into regular JavaScript numbers, which lose precision above 2^53. The README says scores can be that large and must never be converted to numbers. I confirmed it with two players: 9007199254740992 ranked #1 and 9007199254740993 ranked #2, which is the wrong order. When two scores round to the same number, they keep whatever order they came in. Since `topN` uses `rankings`, it has the same bug.
Fix: use the existing `compareScore` helper in `src/score.js`, which handles scores of any length:
```js
.sort((a, b) => compareScore(b.score, a.score))
```
Please also add a test with two scores above 2^53 that differ only in the last digit. The current test uses only small scores, so it can't catch this.

**Worth considering (not blocking)**
• **Ties:** players with equal scores get different ranks (1, 2) based on input order. If ties should share a rank, that needs deciding now. If not, add a tie-breaker so the order doesn't depend on input.
• **`displayName`:** it crashes if `player.name` is missing (null or undefined). `(player.name ?? '').trim()` handles that, if missing names can happen.
• **`topN`:** it has no tests, and negative or non-integer `n` values give odd results. Also, the commit message says "paginate," but there's only top-N.

The version bump to 1.1.0, the changelog and the README updates all look fine.
